column1: # shahrah shard-hash test vectors. Frozen -- see docs/HASH.md.
# Generated once from the reference C implementation of XXH3-64
# (libxxhash 0.8.3) with the canonical encoding of docs/HASH.md applied
# independently of crates/hash. A failing test means the code changed,
# never that this file needs regenerating.
# Tab-separated. Skip blank lines and lines beginning with '#'.
# version    hash version tag; only 1 exists
# type       postgres type of the key
# value      the input, in the natural form for its type:
#              int2/int4/int8/oid  decimal, may be negative
#              uuid                canonical hyphenated lowercase
#              text/bytea          lowercase hex of the raw bytes
# canonical  lowercase hex of the exact bytes handed to XXH3-64
# hash       the 64-bit XXH3 result, 16 lowercase hex digits
# shard      the low 16 bits of hash, decimal, 0..65535
# version
# integers: the widening rule. int2/int4/int8 of the same value must
# produce identical canonical bytes and therefore the same shard.
# integer boundaries. -1 and the MIN values are where a zero-extension
# or endianness bug shows up first.
# oid widens UNSIGNED. oid 4294967295 and int4 -1 share the same 32-bit
# pattern but are different keys -- that is the rule being pinned here.
# uuid: the 16 raw bytes, never the hyphenated string. The value column
# holds the hyphenated form precisely so the test has to do the parse.
# text: XXH3 dispatches on length. These sit on both sides of every
# internal boundary -- 3, 8, 16, 128, 240 bytes.
# text: UTF-8 is the canonical form, and no normalization happens here.
# "Ali", "ali" and " ali " are three different keys. That is deliberate.
# bytea: arbitrary bytes, including NUL and sequences that are not
# valid UTF-8. Last row crosses XXH3's 1024-byte block boundary.
# A consequence of using one unseeded hash for every type (D6): a bytea
# holding the UTF-8 bytes of "ali" lands on the same shard as text
# "ali", and a bytea holding 42 little-endian lands with int8 42.
# Harmless -- a column has one type -- but pinned here so it stays a
# known property rather than a surprise.
